definitions.explanation: The deepest, most hidden aspects of a subject or discipline. Often refers to knowledge or truths that are not easily accessible and require deep study to understand.

examples.japanese: {学問|がくもん}の{深奥|しんおう}を{極|きわ}める。
examples.english: To master the profound depths of a discipline.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}の{深奥|しんおう}にはまだ{多|おお}くの{謎|なぞ}がある。
examples.english: There are still many mysteries in the profound depths of nature.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{研究|けんきゅう}を{経|へ}て、ようやく{哲学|てつがく}の{深奥|しんおう}に{触|ふ}れることができた。
examples.english: After years of research, I was finally able to touch upon the deeper mysteries of philosophy.

notes:
{深奥|しんおう} refers to the deepest, most hidden aspects of a subject — the profound mysteries that require deep study to reach.

COMPOUNDS:
{深|しん} (deep) + {奥|おう} (inner depths, recesses).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深奥|しんおう}を{極|きわ}める: to plumb the depths of
- {深奥|しんおう}に{触|ふ}れる: to touch upon the mysteries of
- {学問|がくもん}の{深奥|しんおう}: the profound depths of a discipline
- {自然|しぜん}の{深奥|しんおう}: the mysteries of nature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {深遠|しんえん}: profound, far-reaching (emphasizes depth of thought; used for ideas or philosophy)
- {奥義|おうぎ}: secret teaching, esoteric principle (used in martial arts or traditional arts)

REGISTER:
A literary and formal word. Rarely used in casual conversation. Common in academic writing, philosophy, and essays about the arts.
